summary: Four standalone-ish modules under self_organize.py. memory.py holds EditableMemory: a fixed-slot key/token store with a surprise-gated write, three eviction rules (circular "recency", LFU "usage", LRU-on-retrieval "lru"), an optional per-expert partition, a per-source floor, a probation region for newly-written entries, two adaptive flag predicates (self-consistency "wrong" and reconstruction "unverified") and delete/delete_src/reassign_src/sweep_wrong editing. tokenizer.py holds ByteBPE (offline, unused by the live system) and DynamicTokenizer, an online byte-grounded BPE that mints tokens mid-run from a running pair tally, up to vmax, with an optional novelty re-ranker and a p(b|a) predictability gate that is deliberately fail-open; ids are positional and minting is append-only, which is the invariant remap_mem_ctx depends on. datastream.py is MmapConcat, a read-only virtual concatenation of files presented as one indexable byte sequence, plus open_corpus. world_model.py is a JEPA-style latent forward-dynamics core (WorldEncoder + ForwardModel + VICReg _var_cov) and DynamicsPopulation, a routed population of dynamics predictors with EMA fitness, grow-on-plateau and a soft cull. The recurring defect class here is exactly the one the project names: mechanisms that are armed and structurally cannot fire (the wrong-flag read filter, pressure(), the world-model grow), state that is recorded but not carried across a resume (probation, recon, gate_theta, nsrc_max, tokenizer retirement), and two code paths that answer the same question differently (per-owner vs global eviction, batched vs per-window write, disk vs RAM corpus).

levers.name: MEM_WRONG_READ
levers.effect: 1 = the self-consistency wrong flag excludes entries from EVERY retrieval; 0 = the flag is still reported but does not gate reads. Read directly from os.environ inside EditableMemory.__init__ so the config registry sees the read.

levers.name: MEM_CAP
levers.effect: Number of slots in the store — but only when MEM_PER_EXPERT=0. With the partition on it is discarded in favour of n_own*quota.
levers.evidence: self_organize.py:4868; memory.py:36 `if self.n_own > 1: cap = self.n_own * self.quota`

levers.name: MEM_PER_EXPERT
levers.effect: Turns on the per-owner partition (n_own = min(FAB_NMAX, MEM_OWNERS)). Also silently switches off probation, the per-source floor, and the pressure() counters, because the per-owner _store path returns before all of them.

levers.name: MEM_OWNERS
levers.effect: Number of memory partitions, folded down from expert id space (expert_id % n_own). Sets n_own = min(FAB_NMAX, MEM_OWNERS).

levers.name: MEM_QUOTA
levers.effect: Entries per owner block. With MEM_PER_EXPERT on this, not MEM_CAP, determines the store size.

levers.name: EVICT
levers.effect: 'recency' = circular FIFO on write order, 'usage' = LFU on decayed retrieval mass, 'lru' = least-recently-retrieved. Only 'usage' and 'lru' reach the probation/floor machinery, and only when the store is full.

levers.name: MEM_PROBE_EVERY
levers.effect: How often the training loop issues real reads against the store. Zero makes `use` and `last` constants, which turns EVICT=lru/usage into write-order eviction and makes probation promotion impossible.

levers.name: MEM_PROBE_N
levers.effect: Rows per probe read. Bounds how many entries can be promoted out of probation per probe.

levers.name: MEM_SRC_FLOOR
levers.effect: Fraction of cap reserved across live sources; floor_i = src_floor*cap/live. 0 disables protection entirely. Only consulted on the global sampled-eviction path.

levers.name: MEM_PROB_FRAC
levers.effect: Share of the store the never-retrieved (probation) region may occupy before eviction narrows to it. At this system's write:read ratio it is permanently exceeded, so the probation branch is the rule rather than the exception.

levers.name: MEM_PRESSURE
levers.effect: Threshold on pressure() (share of evictions destroying promoted entries) above which a capacity warning prints. Cannot be reached while probation is over budget.

levers.name: MEM_PRESSURE_ACT
levers.effect: 1 turns the pressure warning into an actual fabric-growth trigger (fabgrow.note_shift). Default 0 = report only.

levers.name: WRITE_GATE
levers.effect: Fixed surprise threshold; an item is stored only if 1 - p_model(true token) >= this. Used only when WRITE_ADAPTIVE=0. Also the seed value of gate_theta.

levers.name: WRITE_ADAPTIVE
levers.effect: Turns on the self-calibrating gate. Registry default 0, which leaves both the additive controller and the quantile gate dead.

levers.name: WRITE_QUANTILE
levers.effect: Honours WRITE_TARGET by quantile instead of an absolute threshold. Nested inside the adaptive branch, so it is inert unless WRITE_ADAPTIVE=1.

levers.name: WRITE_TARGET
levers.effect: Target kept-write fraction for the adaptive/quantile gate.

levers.name: USE_DECAY / DECAY_EVERY
levers.effect: Multiplicative decay of the retrieval-count vector, applied once every DECAY_EVERY WRITES (not per step, not per read).

levers.name: TOPK
levers.effect: Neighbours per retrieval; also the width of the hit/weight tensors read() returns (both discarded by every product call site).

levers.name: WRONG_SWEEP
levers.effect: 1 deletes every currently-flagged-wrong entry at the end of the run. Default 0 — but 0 does NOT make the flag inert, because read() filters on the same predicate.

levers.name: VERIFY / VERIFY_SWEEP
levers.effect: VERIFY=recon builds a Reconstructor and populates mem.recon at the end of the run, activating is_unverified(); VERIFY_SWEEP additionally deletes those entries. Default VERIFY=selfcon leaves recon all -1 and is_unverified() a no-op.

levers.name: TOK_ONLINE
levers.effect: 1 = mint throughout training (model sized to VMAX, corpora stay bytes); 0 = build the vocabulary up front, tokenize the corpora once, and set V to the achieved vocab size.

levers.name: VMAX
levers.effect: Softmax width AND the tokenizer's hard mint ceiling. On a resume the tokenizer's saved vmax travels with the file and must be explicitly raised to match a widened emb/head.

levers.name: MIN_PAIR
levers.effect: Minimum pair count to be mintable. Registry default 50; the tokenizer module's own default is 200. On a LOAD the value comes from the saved json and the env variable is ignored.

levers.name: MAX_TOK
levers.effect: Maximum bytes per minted token. A candidate exceeding it is skipped (gate_skipped). On a LOAD the value comes from the saved json.

levers.name: TOK_DROPOUT
levers.effect: Probability of skipping a merge during count=True segmentation, letting byte-level material through. Draws from the GLOBAL random module. On a LOAD the value comes from the saved json.

levers.name: TOK_MINT_PMIN
levers.effect: Minimum p(b|a) for a merge to pass the predictability gate; 0 = mint on frequency alone. Read from os.environ inside __init__ AND mirrored from self_organize on the fresh-construct path only.

levers.name: TOK_MINT_GATE_K
levers.effect: How far down the frequency ranking the predictability gate may look. Deliberately generous (1024) so the window is not itself the limiter.

levers.name: TOK_MINT_NOVEL / TOK_MINT_NOVEL_K
levers.effect: Re-ranks the top candidates by growth since last look, (c-seen)/(1+seen)^novel, so minting follows NEW material. 0 reproduces plain most-frequent minting. Turning it on also destroys the frequency ordering the min_pair early-exit and the gate_forced fallback assume.

levers.name: GROW_EVERY / GROW_BURST
levers.effect: Cadence and burst size of maybe_grow calls during training; together with the run length they, not VMAX, often decide how full the vocabulary gets.

levers.name: TOK_PROBATION / TOK_PROBATION_STEPS / TOK_PROBATION_BY / TOK_PROBATION_MIN
levers.effect: Appearances a minted token must earn (or a deadline to earn them by) before it is kept; failures are retire()d. Default 0 = the whole path, including retire(), never runs.

levers.name: TOKENIZER_PATH
levers.effect: Which vocabulary file indexes the checkpoint's embedding rows. Unset on a resume it now prefers <RESUME>.dyntok.json over the shared data/dyntok.json. Loading from it also imports that file's min_pair/max_tok/dropout/max_pairs.

levers.name: DISK_STREAM
levers.effect: mmap the corpus instead of reading it into RAM. Also changes what the held-out set IS (VAL_CAP-truncated slice of the mmap vs the full RAM tail), and enables per-epoch resampling.

levers.name: CORPUS_CAP
levers.effect: Per-domain byte cap. On the disk path it stops opening files and clips total; on the RAM path it slices the concatenated bytes.

levers.name: DOMAINS / DATA_DIR
levers.effect: Which per-domain corpora are opened and in what index order. CORP and DN must stay index-aligned; the 5000-byte drop filter re-aligns both.

levers.name: WORLD_MODEL
levers.effect: Builds WorldEncoder + DynamicsPopulation (+ world_proj under WORLD_FEEDBACK) and adds the latent forward-prediction and anti-collapse terms to the loss.

levers.name: WORLD_GROW
levers.effect: Enables grow-on-plateau and soft_cull of the dynamics population on the MANAGE_EVERY cadence. Explicitly ANDed with WORLD_MODEL because its step hook dereferences world_fwd outside the WORLD_MODEL block.

levers.name: WORLD_N0 / WORLD_NMAX
levers.effect: Starting and maximum number of dynamics predictors. NMAX also sizes the fit/mass/alive buffers and is what a resume's grow-replay loop must be able to reach.

levers.name: WORLD_K
levers.effect: Prediction horizon in positions: z[:, :-K] predicts z[:, K:]. Changes what 'the next latent' means without changing anything the loss reports.

levers.name: WORLD_W / WORLD_VAR
levers.effect: Weights on the population forward-prediction term and on the encoder anti-collapse term respectively; WORLD_VAR is applied at full strength because under-weighting it produced latent collapse.

carry_forward.item: Minting is APPEND-ONLY and ids are positional. id2bytes[i] must never change meaning, and no id may ever be removed or renumbered.
carry_forward.why: Three separate mechanisms depend on it: remap_mem_ctx re-segments every stored memory context and is only exact because an entry's bytes can always be recovered; DynamicTokenizer.load replays merges in order and every later token is built on earlier indices; and the LM's emb/head rows are indexed by token id across resumes. This is why retire() is soft rather than a removal.
carry_forward.evidence: tokenizer.py:409-411; self_organize.py:3225-3227 'The remap is exact in id space because minting is APPEND-ONLY'; tokenizer.py:483-487

carry_forward.item: cap is DERIVED from the partition. Setting MEM_PER_EXPERT=1 discards MEM_CAP in favour of n_own*quota.
carry_forward.why: At the defaults this is a 24x reduction in store size (200000 -> 8192) and every memory result scales with it. The startup warning exists precisely because this was invisible.

carry_forward.item: nsrc is the per-source floor's ONLY input, and `has = (nsrc > 0)` is what makes a source eligible for protection at all. Any path that sets `active` directly must call rebuild_census().
carry_forward.why: The resume path bypassed _commit and left nsrc at zeros, silently disabling MEM_SRC_FLOOR for the whole run while the banner kept printing 'src floor 0.5'. A source whose count has drifted to zero is unprotected by the very floor that exists to stop it being driven to zero.

carry_forward.item: ONE SLOT, ONE ROW. Any code path that builds an eviction `idx` must not name a slot twice.
carry_forward.why: Index assignment collapses a repeat silently (later row wins), so the store reports more writes than it holds; worse, _commit decrements the displaced source once per occurrence while crediting the new source idx.numel() times, which drove a per-source count to -2 against a peak of 111230. The dedup in _commit is the backstop and n_dup_slot is how a third producer stays visible.

carry_forward.item: `last` is the USE clock and must be stamped by BOTH write and read. It was once gated on n_own>1, so on the global store it stayed all-zero for entire runs and any rule consulting it chose arbitrarily.
carry_forward.why: Write-recency evicts a domain that has gone quiet by construction; use-recency evicts a domain nothing is asking for. That distinction is the whole reason the store has a floor and a probe at all.

carry_forward.item: EVICT=lru/usage are only real if reads HAPPEN during training. Without MEM_PROBE_EVERY, `use` stays 0 and `last` stays at write time, and both rules degenerate to FIFO regardless of what EVICT says.
carry_forward.why: Before the read probe existed, mem.read() was called only from generate() and bpb_true() — both eval — so every run in the project that claimed retrieval-based eviction was doing write-order eviction.

carry_forward.item: Writes compartmentalise, READS stay global. An expert's memory is its own to keep and to lose, but any query must still be able to reach it.
carry_forward.why: This is the 'partially, not fully, isolate' property the per-owner partition exists to provide. A future change that scopes reads to the querying owner would destroy the only mechanism by which information mixes across experts.

carry_forward.item: The per-owner _store path is a SECOND, independent eviction implementation. It shares only _commit with the global path, and it implements neither probation nor the per-source floor.
carry_forward.why: Every future fix to eviction has to be applied twice or deliberately not applied twice, and every report that reads src_report() / pressure() must state which path produced the numbers.

carry_forward.item: There are TWO write paths and only one carries the owner: write_batch(owners=...) honours the partition, write() cannot. Which one runs is decided by KEY_PREGATE / KEY_BATCH / KEY_SRC — knobs about key ENCODING, not about memory ownership.
carry_forward.why: At the defaults (1/1/model) the partition is honoured, so this is latent. It becomes live the moment anything pushes the run onto the fallback, and nothing else in the run would say so.

carry_forward.item: Memory source ids and assembler domain ids share ONE namespace, and no id is reserved. The wrongness injection's src=99 is a collision waiting for a run whose assembler reaches 99 domains.
carry_forward.why: delete_src(99) then deletes real material, and the precision/recall figures reported for the wrongness detector are computed against a contaminated positive set.
carry_forward.evidence: self_organize.py:8880, 8884, 8945; memory.py:381 records 125 source ids on a real run

carry_forward.item: The wrong flag gates RETRIEVAL, not just deletion. 'Detect-only' (WRONG_SWEEP=0) does not make it inert — read() filters on the same predicate.
carry_forward.why: 63,146 genuine entries were flagged at 3% precision out of 200,000 active, i.e. about a third of the store unreachable, while the log printed 'sweep OFF ... too low to delete safely' and read as reassurance. MEM_WRONG_READ is the knob that separates detecting from acting.

carry_forward.item: A gate must be MEASURED WHERE IT GATES, not from the state left at the end of the run. Every write resets that entry's selfcon to -1, so an end-of-run snapshot of the flag says nothing about what any read actually saw.
carry_forward.why: The first version of the DID IT FIRE row for this gate armed on `(selfcon >= 0).sum() > 10` at report time and printed 'read() filters nothing' in the same report as '61,952 of 200,000 active entries are excluded from EVERY retrieval'. Both were honestly computed; only one was about what happened.

carry_forward.item: The probation region's 10% budget is not achievable at this system's write:read ratio, so pressure() reads ~0 whatever the store is suffering. Treat it as unavailable, not as a healthy signal.
carry_forward.why: A pilot wrote 11.7M times into 200k slots against 1469 read probes; probation was 82% of the store, permanently over budget, so eviction always took the probation branch and n_main_evict stayed near zero.

carry_forward.item: Probation decides WHICH POOL is drawn from; the floor decides who inside it is off limits. Both questions have to be asked — narrowing to probation and going straight to the ranking cancelled the floor and took a domain-switch test from 49 survivors back to 0.
carry_forward.why: It is the one place in the code where two protective mechanisms compose rather than override, and the composition order is load-bearing.

carry_forward.item: The predictability gate may REORDER what gets minted and may never PREVENT it. Dead softmax rows are the worst failure this system has, so a quality filter that creates them is strictly worse than no filter.
carry_forward.why: Measured: gated minting decelerated and stopped at 1439 of 2048, leaving 609 rows (29.7% of the width) never minted, and the run scored 3.600 b/B against an ungated ~1.96. Both the gate_forced fallback and the mintable-walk exist to enforce this.

carry_forward.item: A rejected CANDIDATE is not an exhausted VOCABULARY. maybe_grow returning None is read by every caller as 'stop the burst', so the max_tok / already-exists rejection must walk on rather than return None.
carry_forward.why: Measured: max_tok=16 vmax=2048 stalled at 1845/2048 with 3940 pairs still above min_pair; max_tok=6 vmax=4000 stalled at 658/4000 with 1866 still above. mint_rescued and mint_widened exist so the repair's own firing is distinguishable from a run where the hole was never in the path.

carry_forward.item: The tokenizer file carries its own vmax, min_pair, max_tok, dropout and max_pairs. Only vmax is repaired on resume; the rest silently override the environment.
carry_forward.why: A tokenizer saved full at vmax=2048 comes back full and refuses every candidate before a candidate is even formed — a new area gets new experts and no tokens. The same shape applies to MIN_PAIR and MAX_TOK and is not yet handled.

carry_forward.item: soft_cull must not run in the same cadence block as grow, and grow must initialise the new predictor's mass, or every growth is undone immediately.
carry_forward.why: This is the generic 'a new unit cannot survive a competition scored on evidence it has not had time to gather' failure that memory.py's probation comment names as ONE problem occurring three times over in this project — and the world model is the fourth instance, without the protection.

carry_forward.item: Soft-culling a world-model predictor is one-way: alive is only ever set to 0, never back to 1, and grow() still counts dead slots against nmax.
carry_forward.why: Both docstrings call it reversible, so a future reader will assume a revival path exists. It does not, in either module.
carry_forward.evidence: world_model.py:82, 109, 121-128; grep for alive[ over the live tree returns only reads plus the single 0.0 write

carry_forward.item: mem.pos is a byte offset into the TRAINING STREAM, not into any corpus file, and source.bin is the stream that was current at checkpoint time.
carry_forward.why: Under DISK_STREAM the stream is rebuilt per epoch while memory persists, so grounded recall for pre-final-epoch entries reads unrelated text. The narrower version of this (windows queued across an epoch boundary) is already fixed and documented; the store-wide version is not.

carry_forward.item: Under DISK_STREAM the held-out tail STAYS inside CORP. SEG_LEN, computed in self_organize, is the only thing keeping training off it.
carry_forward.why: datastream.py's own docstring advertises len(CORP[p]) as part of the interface, which under that mode is the whole corpus including the eval set.

carry_forward.item: MAX_DOMAINS is read with default 32 when sizing the memory census and with default FAB_NMAX (4096) everywhere else; this is only legal because it is in _DERIVED and therefore exempt from _env's default-mismatch refusal.
carry_forward.why: It is the one surviving instance of exactly the disagreement _env exists to make impossible, and it is what fixes n_src_hint at 64 while real runs reach 125 source ids. _commit's table growth is the only reason it self-heals.
carry_forward.evidence: self_organize.py:4874 vs 598; exemption at self_organize.py:90/95/520; growth at memory.py:478-482

carry_forward.item: torch.unique SORTS, so a de-duplicated candidate pool must be re-permuted before a topk whose ties resolve toward the earlier position — otherwise low-numbered slots systematically lose every tie, and under EVICT=usage ties are the common case (every never-retrieved entry has use=0).
carry_forward.why: A non-obvious interaction between two library behaviours that silently turns a uniform sample into a biased one; the permutation costs nothing on a few hundred indices.
